title: Get or renew a local business license (BPOL)
question: I am starting or running a business in Staunton. How do I get a business license, and when must I renew it?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue, City of Staunton (an elected constitutional officer, who assesses and issues business licenses; the City Treasurer collects payments)
summary: Staunton requires a business license from the Commissioner of the Revenue for each business and each location in the city, including home-based, part-time and 1099 work. First get zoning approval (a Home Occupation Permit if you work from home) and any SCC, state license or health approvals; if you sell alcohol, tell the Commissioner once you have your ABC license. Then mail, fax or email the Business License Application with your estimated gross receipts. The city asks for it within 30 days of opening; state law says before you open. Up to $50,000 in gross receipts the license costs $30; above that a rate by class applies (retail $0.20 per $100). Licenses run by calendar year and are renewed by March 1. The city's renewal form charges 10% for late filing, plus 10% yearly interest.

steps.step: Check whether your business needs a Staunton business license, and how many
steps.how: You need a City of Staunton business license if you have a definite place of business in the city (an office or location used for business for 30 consecutive days or more), or if you have no place of business anywhere and live in Staunton, so a home-based business is covered. Peddlers, itinerant merchants and state-licensed contractors working in the city also need one. The city says part-time and hobby businesses, and people paid on a 1099 as independent contractors, need a license too; state law defines a business as a continuous and regular course of dealing for a livelihood or profit, not an irregular or isolated transaction. State law requires a separate license for each business and each location. A person with two or more businesses at the same place may instead elect one license for all of them, if each is licensable there, all are taxed at the same rate or the licensee accepts the highest rate, and the licensee gives the Commissioner the information it asks for (the city's pages do not mention this). An out-of-town contractor needs a Staunton license only when its work in the city exceeds $25,000 in a calendar year. Some receipts are exempt under state law, for example those of 501(c)(3) charities (except unrelated business income) and farm products sold by the person who grew them.
steps.quote: Even if you conduct business on a part-time basis, or hobby related basis, you are required to obtain a license.

steps.step: Get zoning approval, and a Home Occupation Permit if you work from home
steps.who: Business owner, applying to the Community Development Department's Planning & Zoning Division
steps.how: The city requires zoning approval for any business. Check with Planning & Zoning that your location is zoned for the use. If you run the business from your home, apply for a Home Occupation Permit online in the city's permitting portal or on the paper form. Include a permission letter if you do not own and live in the home. Review takes about five business days, and the permit is emailed to you once it is approved. A new location, or a move, may need its own zoning approval, and some uses need an occupancy permit. The permit section links to the Planning & Zoning fee schedule, which lists a Zoning Permit Fee of $50.00 but no separate home occupation fee; ask Planning & Zoning which fee applies.
steps.deadline: Before applying for the business license
steps.fee: Not stated for the Home Occupation Permit; the linked Planning & Zoning fee schedule lists a Zoning Permit Fee of $50.00 (see fees)
steps.quote: Home based businesses are required to apply for a home occupancy permit prior to applying for a business license.

steps.step: Register your business name or entity, and get any state license or permit your trade needs
steps.who: Business owner; State Corporation Commission (SCC); Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR) or the relevant state board; Virginia Department of Health; Virginia ABC; Virginia Department of Taxation
steps.how: If you use a trade name (a "doing business as" name) instead of your legal name, register it with the SCC as a fictitious name. The city's instructions say businesses that have incorporated (LLC, Inc., S-Corp, partnerships and the like) must be registered with the SCC and must include the certificate of good standing or registration certificate; sole proprietors need not register with the SCC. Contractors need a current state contractor's license. Realtors, brokers, barbers, hair stylists, nail technicians, estheticians, tattoo artists and other regulated trades need an active DPOR license, and doctors, nurses and massage therapists need their state board licensure. A food service business needs a health permit. Sellers of taxable goods must register for Virginia sales tax. Have an FEIN, or your Social Security number if you do not need an FEIN. Every contractor must also certify in writing, at each application and renewal, that it complies with Virginia's workers' compensation law (coverage is needed where that law requires it); the renewal form asks for Form 61A or insurance the office can verify. Copies of these registrations and licenses go with the application.
steps.deadline: Before the business license can be issued
steps.quote: A copy of the registration must be provided to our office before a business license can be issued.

steps.how: The Commissioner will not issue a license while the applicant owes delinquent business license or personal property taxes to the city. If you are not sure whether you owe anything, ask the Treasurer's office (540-332-3833) and pay any balance first.
steps.deadline: Before the business license can be issued
steps.quote: No business license will be issued until all delinquent business license and personal property taxes owed by the applicant to the City of Staunton have been paid (VA Code 58.1-3700).

steps.step: Find your license classification and estimate your gross receipts
steps.who: Business owner; the Commissioner of the Revenue can confirm the class and rate
steps.how: Pick your classification from the table on the back of the application (contractor, retail, professional, business service, direct seller, wholesale merchant). Then estimate your gross receipts from the day you start until the end of the calendar year. Gross receipts are all income before expenses; sales tax, local excise taxes, and returns and allowances are excluded. Up to $50,000 the license costs $30. Above $50,000, multiply the estimate by the rate for your class. If you are unsure of your class, call the Commissioner's office.
steps.fee: $30 for gross receipts of $0-$50,000; above $50,000, the classification rate per $100 of gross receipts (see fees)
steps.quote: If you are unsure of the classification of your business, please call the Commissioner of the Revenue to determine both the business classification and rate.

steps.step: Submit the Business License Application to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.who: Business owner, filing with the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Fill in the Business License Application: trade and legal names, business location, business type, SSN or FEIN, sales tax number, any contractor or DPOR license number, a description of the business, its classification, your estimate of gross receipts and the tax due. Then sign it. The PDF has no fillable fields, so print it. Attach the documents from steps 2 and 3. Mail it to P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402, fax it to 540-851-4022, or email it to revenue@ci.staunton.va.us. No page offers an online application for a new business: the online service is for paying, with online renewal being added for existing accounts. The city's pages say to file within 30 days of starting business, while state law says to apply before you begin.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of when you begin to conduct business (city); state law says prior to beginning business
steps.quote: To avoid penalties and interest, you are required to file an application within 30 days of when you begin to conduct business.

steps.step: Pay the license fee or tax
steps.who: Business owner; the City Treasurer collects payment
steps.how: The application asks you to calculate the total tax due, and its office-use box records payment, so expect to pay when you apply. Make checks payable to the City of Staunton. You can pay at the Treasurer's office (City Hall, 1st floor; cash, check or card, with a fee for card payments), mail a check or money order to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 474, put it in the green city drop box on Central Avenue under the clock tower, or pay online through the city's self-service portal. Online payment needs a web user account that the Commissioner's office links to your business license account: email revenue@ci.staunton.va.us with your account email and license account number.
steps.fee: As calculated on the application (see fees); card payments carry a fee
steps.quote: Payments by cash and/or credit card can be made in-person with the Treasurer's office; a fee is charged for credit card payments.

steps.step: If you sell alcohol, tell the Commissioner when you get your ABC license
steps.who: Business owner; Virginia ABC; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Apply to Virginia ABC for the state license. When it is issued, notify the Commissioner of the Revenue. A separate local ABC license tax is then added to your business license. It is prorated monthly; the charges the city lists run from $40 to $500 by license type, and the city says not every ABC charge is listed.
steps.deadline: When the ABC license is obtained
steps.fee: Local ABC license tax by license type, prorated monthly (see fees)
steps.quote: Businesses must notify the Commissioner of the Revenue when an ABC license is obtained.

steps.step: Renew the license every year by March 1
steps.who: Licensee; the Commissioner of the Revenue mails a renewal notice
steps.how: The license runs for the calendar year and expires on December 31. The Commissioner mails each current licensee a renewal form. On it, report last year's gross receipts for each license class, apply the rate, and enter the tax due. Contractors attach copies of paid licenses from other localities so they can deduct those receipts, and confirm workers' compensation coverage (Form 61A, or insurance the office can verify). Sign and return the form; the renewal and the payment must both be submitted or postmarked by March 1. Online renewal is being added, but a business in its second or third year may only be able to pay online, not file.
steps.deadline: Filing and payment by March 1 of the license year (the 2026 form: submitted and/or postmarked by March 1, 2026); when March 1 is a weekend day or a holiday, state law allows the next business day (Va. Code § 1-210(E))
steps.fee: Per the classification and rates table (see fees)
steps.quote: The renewal and payment must be submitted and/or postmarked by March 1, 2026.

steps.step: At your first renewal, report actual gross receipts and settle the difference
steps.who: Licensee in its first renewal; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: A new business was licensed on an estimate. On the first renewal, report the actual gross receipts for the first year, and an estimate for the new year. If the actual receipts were higher than the estimate, you may get a bill for more tax for the first year. If they were lower, you may get a credit on the new license. The office will help with the calculation.
steps.quote: If you exceeded the estimated amount, you may receive a bill for an additional tax due for 2025.

steps.step: If you cannot file on time, ask for an extension; otherwise expect a 10% penalty and interest
steps.how: State law lets the Commissioner extend the filing time for reasonable cause, possibly on condition that you pay a reasonable estimate of the tax. Without an extension, the 2026 renewal form says a filing received or postmarked after March 1 is late, that a 10% penalty will be assessed as of March 2 and interest at 10% a year as of April 1. State law says a 10% penalty may be imposed, and that when both the filing and the payment are late only the late-filing penalty is charged, unless the Commissioner finds a history of noncompliance. When a due date falls on a weekend, a holiday or a day the office is closed, state law allows the filing on the next business day (March 1, 2026 was a Sunday; see caveats). If the lateness was not your fault, ask for the penalty to be waived or abated (see escalation).
steps.quote: The assessing official may grant an extension of time in which to file an application for a license, for reasonable cause.

steps.step: Keep records of your gross receipts
steps.how: Keep records that show your gross receipts for each license year. They must be open to the Commissioner's inspection. If you never applied, or in case of fraud, state law says the Commissioner shall assess the omitted tax for the current license year and the six preceding years.
steps.quote: Every person who is assessable with a local license tax shall keep sufficient records to enable the assessor to verify the correctness of the tax paid for the license years assessable

steps.step: Close the license when you stop doing business in Staunton
steps.who: Licensee, writing to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Tell the Commissioner's office in writing that the business has closed, with the closing date and your signature. You can also complete box (1) of the renewal form with the date you stopped, sign it and return it.
steps.quote: In order to close your business license, you must notify our office in writing that you have ceased to operate your business and provide a closing date and a signature.

escalation.trigger: Unsure how the license tax or a classification applies to your business
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (written ruling; give all the relevant facts)
escalation.quote: Any taxpayer or authorized representative of a taxpayer may request a written ruling regarding the application of a local license tax to a specific situation from the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Cannot file the application or renewal by the due date, for reasonable cause
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (ask for an extension; you may have to pay a reasonable estimate of the tax)
escalation.quote: The assessing official may grant an extension of time in which to file an application for a license, for reasonable cause.

escalation.trigger: Late filing or payment penalty charged although the lateness was not your fault
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (for a late filing penalty) or City Treasurer (for a late payment penalty it imposed): ask for abatement and show you acted responsibly and that events beyond your control caused the lateness
escalation.quote: If the failure to file or pay was not the fault of the taxpayer, the penalties shall not be imposed, or if imposed, shall be abated by the official who assessed them.

escalation.trigger: License refused because delinquent city business license or personal property taxes are owed
escalation.next: City Treasurer (pay or resolve the balance, then reapply); a dispute over the underlying tax follows that tax's own appeal route
escalation.quote: may require that no business license under this chapter shall be issued until the applicant has produced satisfactory evidence that all delinquent business license, real estate, personal property, meals, transient occupancy, severance and admissions taxes owed by the business to the county, city or town have been paid

escalation.trigger: License held up because a trade name has not been registered
escalation.next: State Corporation Commission (file the certificate of assumed or fictitious name, then give the Commissioner a copy)
escalation.quote: No license shall be issued by a commissioner of the revenue until a certificate of assumed or fictitious name has been made and filed (i) in the office of the clerk of the Commission

escalation.trigger: Assessment increased, refund denied, tax assessed where none was before, tax estimated when no application was filed, or an amended application's correction denied (an appealable event)
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue, by written administrative appeal (identify the taxpayer, tax periods, amount in dispute, remedy sought, each alleged error and the grounds)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year assessed, or within one year from the appealable event, whichever is later
escalation.quote: may file an administrative appeal of the assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event, whichever is later, with the commissioner of the revenue or other local assessing official.

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the classification of your business
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (administrative appeal of the classification)
escalation.deadline: At any time (but this does not extend the limits for appealing an assessment)
escalation.quote: The taxpayer may at any time also file an administrative appeal of the classification applicable to the taxpayer's business

escalation.trigger: A timely and complete administrative appeal is pending
escalation.next: Collection of the disputed amount is suspended until the Commissioner's final determination (interest still accrues, no further penalty), unless the Treasurer finds that collection would be jeopardized by delay, or the Commissioner reports that you have not answered a request for relevant information after a reasonable time or that the appeal is frivolous
escalation.quote: collection activity with respect to the amount in dispute relating to any assessment by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official shall be suspended until a final determination is issued by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: No final determination after the appeal has been pending more than one year
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation), after at least 30 days' written notice to the Commissioner of the Revenue
escalation.deadline: After more than one year without a decision, on at least 30 days' written notice
escalation.quote: elect to treat the appeal as denied and appeal the assessment or classification of the taxpayer's business to the Tax Commissioner in accordance with the provisions of subdivision 6

escalation.trigger: The Commissioner of the Revenue's determination is adverse
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation); serve a copy of the appeal on the Commissioner of the Revenue
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days of the date of the Commissioner of the Revenue's determination; the Tax Commissioner decides within 90 days of receipt unless both sides are told it will take longer
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment or determination to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the date of the determination by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Notice of intent to appeal to the Tax Commissioner given
escalation.next: Collection of the disputed amount is suspended until the Tax Commissioner's final determination, if the appeal is filed and served within 30 days of the notice (interest still accrues, no further penalty), unless collection would be jeopardized by delay, you have not answered a request for relevant information, or the appeal is frivolous
escalation.deadline: Appeal filed and served within 30 days of the notice of intent
escalation.quote: collection activity with respect to the amount in dispute relating to any assessment by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official shall be suspended until a final determination is issued by the Tax Commissioner

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved after the Tax Commissioner's determination, or choosing to go straight to court
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court (the application names the "City of Staunton"; the city attorney defends)
escalation.deadline: Whichever is latest: three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, one year from the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or one year from a final determination under § 58.1-3981
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

escalation.trigger: Licensed in several localities whose methods would tax more than 100% of your gross receipts, and no apportionment agreement is reached
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue first: tell it that the localities' methods conflict, and it must make a good faith effort to reach an apportionment agreement with the other localities. If none is reached, either you or the Commissioner may ask the Department of Taxation for an advisory opinion, with notice to the other.
escalation.quote: either the assessor or taxpayer may seek an advisory opinion from the Department of Taxation pursuant to § 58.1-3701

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act. The 2027 renewal form will carry new dates.

Local law. The Staunton City Code is now published on eCode360 (General Code). Its terms forbid reproducing the text, and the City Code page still links the older codepublishing.com site. So no Code text was read there. The only local-law quotes are from § 5.05.170 as the city's own Business License & Taxes page reproduces it. That reproduction stops after "required to pay annually:" and goes straight to the tax rates. It leaves out the license-fee part of the section, so the $30 fee and the $50,000 floor come from the city's forms and brochure, not from ordinance text. Article II's sections on due dates, penalties, interest, extensions and appeals were not read, and their numbers are not known.

New business deadline. The Start a Business page and the new business brochure say to apply within 30 days of beginning business. State law (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a)) says to apply before beginning business, and lets the locality set payment of a gross-receipts tax at 30 or more days after beginning business (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(b)). The safe course is to apply before opening.

When a new business pays. No page says outright when a new business pays. The application asks for the total tax due and has an office-use payment box, which suggests payment with the application. Ask the office. State law says the tax on a license not based on gross receipts is paid with the application (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(b)); whether the city treats its $30 fee that way is not stated.

Penalty notice on the application. State law requires the forms to state the due date and the late-filing penalty. The new business application (created August 2024) states neither, and the Start a Business page mentions "penalties and interest" without amounts. Only the 2026 renewal form states the 10% penalty and 10% interest.

Weekend due date. March 1, 2026 was a Sunday. The 2026 renewal form says filings received or postmarked after March 1 are late and the penalty is assessed as of March 2, 2026. State law says that when a date set by a local governing body falls on a Saturday, Sunday, legal holiday or a day the office is closed, the act may be performed on the next business day (§ 1-210(E)), and the Commissioner's Taxes page says payments are then accepted the next business day without penalty. So a 2026 renewal filed or paid on Monday, March 2 should not have been penalized; if it was, ask for abatement. March 1, 2027 is a Monday.

Fee and tax above $50,000. The forms show "$0-50,000 $30 fee" and, over $50,000, a rate per $100 of gross receipts. They do not say whether the rate then applies to all gross receipts, as § 5.05.170's "all the gross receipts" reads, or only to receipts above $50,000. Section 58.1-3703(A) says the tax is not collected on gross receipts on which a license fee is charged. Ask the Commissioner how the tax is computed just above $50,000.

Population band. The $50 fee cap and the $50,000 tax floor apply because Staunton has between 25,000 and 50,000 people by the 2020 Census, per §§ 58.1-3703(A) and 58.1-3706(A). Staunton is close to 25,000, and the statute allows the Weldon Cooper Center estimate. Below 25,000 the cap would be $30, and the statutory $50,000 floor would not apply by its terms. The city's $30 fee is within either cap.

Wholesale rates. Staunton's wholesale merchant tax ($100 minimum; $0.50 per $100 of purchases from $10,001 to $50,000, then $0.12) is above the 5 cents per $100 cap in § 58.1-3716. That section lets a locality keep a higher rate it had on January 1, 1964. Whether Staunton's rate is grandfathered, and how the $100 minimum fits the fee cap and the $50,000 floor, was not checked.

Classification names differ. The forms' "Professional (State licensed, i.e. - Real Estate Agent, Doctor)" class carries the ordinance rate for "financial, real estate and professional services". The forms' "Business Service" class carries the rate for "repair, personal and business services and all other businesses". The forms give no rate for peddlers or itinerant merchants; state law caps their tax at $500 a year (§ 58.1-3717(C)). For direct sellers the forms give $0.20 per $100 of gross receipts over $4,000; state law caps the rate at 20 cents per $100 of retail sales or 5 cents per $100 of wholesale sales (§ 58.1-3719.1(A)), so a direct seller with wholesale sales should ask which rate applies.

Hobby and part-time work. The brochure says a license is required even for part-time or hobby-related business. State law defines a business as a continuous and regular course of dealing for a livelihood or profit, not an irregular or isolated transaction (§ 58.1-3700.1). Whether an occasional activity is a business is a question of fact; ask the Commissioner, or request a written ruling (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(8)).

One license for several businesses. State law lets a person with two or more businesses at the same place elect one license for all of them, on the conditions in § 58.1-3703.1(A)(1), and every BPOL ordinance must include a provision substantially similar. None of the city pages or forms read mentions this election.

Appeal procedures not published. Section 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(c) requires each locality to post its classification-appeal procedures, and the name and address for appeals, on its website. None of the pages read (Business License & Taxes, Commissioner of Revenue, Taxes, Start a Business) has them. The escalation route here comes from state law. It assumes appeals go to the Commissioner of the Revenue at P.O. Box 4; confirm with the office.

No deadline for the local decision. State law sets no time limit for the Commissioner of the Revenue to decide a license tax appeal. The only remedy for delay is the one-year rule in § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(e).

Refusal of a license. No statute was found that gives a specific appeal from a refusal to issue a license, for example for delinquent taxes, a missing SCC or DPOR document, or missing zoning approval. The practical route is to cure the defect. Court remedies against a refusal are not covered here. Operating without a license does not relieve the tax (§ 58.1-3700(B)), and omitted tax can be assessed for six prior years (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(4)(b)). The local criminal penalty, if any, has not been checked.

Online service. The Pay for Business License Online link leads to a Tyler identity sign-in page, so the portal is not described here. The February 2026 online instructions (document 13539; Internet Archive copy of 2026-06-13) give the same steps as the superseded December 2023 instructions (document 11919): sign up for a self-service account, then ask the Commissioner's office to link your business license account numbers. They cover signing up and linking only. The 2026 renewal form says online renewal is being integrated, and that a business in its second or third year may not be able to file online. No page offers online applications for new businesses.

Card fees. The Treasurer's fee schedule lists 2.35% for real estate and personal property taxes, $2.25 for utilities and $0.25 for eChecks, but does not list business licenses. The renewal form says only that a fee is charged for card payments at the Treasurer's office.

Interest timing. The 2026 renewal form assesses interest from April 1, 2026. This matches the state rule that no interest is charged on a late payment made within 30 days of the due date (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(e)), at the 10% annual cap in § 58.1-3916. The local ordinance text on interest was not read.

Zoning and occupancy. The application says a Home Occupation Permit must be approved before a license can be issued. The 2021 instructions say zoning approval is required for any business. The Start a Business page says an occupancy permit may be required from the Zoning Administrator. The Planning & Zoning fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 2026-05-10) lists a Zoning Permit Fee of $50.00, a Zoning Official Determination Letter at $75.00 and other fees, but no line for a Home Occupation Permit, so the permit fee is not certain. The Home Occupation application PDF could not be read (the Internet Archive copy returns "not found"), so the zoning steps for a business in commercial space are not given here. The Home Occupation regulations are in the City Code (eCode360) and were not read.

Trade names. The Start a Business page says the Clerk of the Circuit Court can help amend or terminate a partnership or trade name. Since 2020, assumed-name certificates are filed with the SCC (§ 59.1-74(B)), so that advice may be out of date. The SCC phone number also differs between the Start a Business page and the forms, so no SCC phone number is recorded; use the SCC website.

Form dates. The application PDF was created in August 2024 and was still linked in July 2026. The instructions date from June 2021 and the brochure from October 2021. The application asks for an SSN when there is no FEIN. That is the form's requirement.

Tax Commissioner appeal form. Virginia Tax's page says a local license tax appeal must contain the information that § 58.1-1821 requires, and that a copy must go to the local assessing officer. It does not say whether its Appeals Form must be used, so that form is not listed. Ruling and local advisory opinion requests use Form Rulings-Fee and may carry a fee. The BPOL regulations it cites (23 VAC 10-500-640 through 790) were not read.

Separate processes not modelled here: Home Occupation Permit and other zoning approvals, SCC assumed-name and entity filings, DPOR and contractor licensing, health permits, Virginia ABC licenses, homestay registration, the business tangible personal property return (due May 1), and meals, transient occupancy and short-term rental taxes, and the Staunton Enterprise Zone, which the Start a Business page says offers local and state tax and fee incentives to new or expanding businesses (contact the Department of Economic Development).

Privacy. The city pages and forms name the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer and Planning & Zoning staff, and link personal staff mailboxes. Those are omitted, including the Treasurer's name from the mailing address. Only office addresses, main office lines, the office fax, the role-shaped revenue@ci.staunton.va.us mailbox (printed on the Commissioner's own application, instructions, renewal and brochure) and official portals are listed. Court judges and the clerk are not named.

removed: legal_basis Va. Code § 58.1-3706(A): the quote was word for word, but it began mid-sentence, after the words "no local license tax ...", so it read as if a tax shall be imposed on businesses below $100,000 or $50,000, the opposite of the statute. Replaced with the statute's next sentence (a business over $100,000, or $50,000, as applicable, may be subject to the tax), which is confirmed in the index text.
corrections: Quotes: all 59 original state-law quotes are in the indexed text of the sections they cite (lexflow check_quotes: 59 of 59), and all 31 original city quotes are in the Internet Archive copies of the cited city pages and PDFs, fetched again by the verifier. The 7 quotes added below are confirmed the same way (final file: 65 state-law quotes matched by check_quotes, 32 city quotes found in the cited pages).

Weekend due date: Va. Code § 1-210(E) lets an act due on a Saturday, Sunday, holiday or office-closed day be done the next business day. March 1, 2026 was a Sunday, so the 2026 form's penalty "as of March 2, 2026" conflicts with state law and with the Taxes page. Added a § 1-210(E) legal_basis quote; s9 deadline, s11, the late-penalty fee entry and the weekend caveat now say so (the caveat had treated it as an open question).

s11: state law says a 10% penalty "may" be imposed, and that only the late-filing penalty is charged when both filing and payment are late unless there is a history of noncompliance (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(d)); added, with a legal_basis quote.
s12: the step said the Commissioner "can" assess omitted tax; § 58.1-3703.1(A)(4)(b) says "shall", for fraud or failure to apply, for the current license year and the six preceding years. Reworded.

s3: § 58.1-3714(B)(2) requires every contractor to certify workers' compensation compliance in writing at each application and renewal, not only where coverage is required; reworded. The SCC registration rule for incorporated businesses and partnerships is now attributed to the city's instructions, which say it.

s1: added the state single-license election for several businesses at one place (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(1)) and the state definition of a business (continuous and regular course of dealing, not an irregular or isolated transaction, § 58.1-3700.1), next to the city's statement that hobby and part-time businesses need a license; three legal_basis quotes and two caveats added.

s2 and fees: the Planning & Zoning fee schedule is in the Internet Archive (copy of 2026-05-10) and was read: it lists a Zoning Permit Fee of $50.00 and no home occupation line. Added a fee entry with that quote, a source, and updated s2's fee and the zoning caveat; the modeller had recorded it as not read.

Form f4 and the online caveat: the February 2026 online instructions (document 13539) are in the Internet Archive (copy of 2026-06-13) and were read; they give the same sign-up and account-linking steps as the 2023 version. Title, fillable (false) and caveat updated; source added.

Escalation: the two collection-suspension rungs now give the statutory exceptions (collection jeopardized by delay, no answer to a request for information, frivolous appeal) from § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(d) and (6)(b); the apportionment rung now says the Commissioner must first try in good faith to reach an apportionment agreement before either side seeks an advisory opinion (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(3)(c)).

Summary: an ABC license is not a prerequisite to the business license (the instructions say to notify the Commissioner once it is obtained); the late charges are attributed to the city's renewal form.
s8: the $40 to $500 range is of the ABC charges the city lists; it says not all are listed.
s9: "return it with payment" replaced by the form's rule that the renewal and payment be submitted or postmarked by March 1.

Caveats: added that state law has a license not based on gross receipts paid with the application (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(b), with a legal_basis quote); that state law caps a direct seller's wholesale sales at 5 cents per $100 while the city's forms give 20 cents (§ 58.1-3719.1(A)); and the Staunton Enterprise Zone incentives on the Start a Business page as a separate process.

Sources: added the 2026-08-09 Internet Archive copy of the Business License & Taxes page (license text unchanged), the 2026 online instructions, the Planning & Zoning fees page and Va. Code § 1-210. Form f6: the Internet Archive lists a 2026-04-13 copy of the Home Occupation application, but it returns not found.

Checked and left as is: Commissioner and Treasurer addresses, phones, fax, hours and the drop box against the Commissioner, Taxes and Paying Taxes & Fees pages; the Circuit Court address, Clerk's Office phone and hours against the live vacourts.gov page; the Virginia Tax appeals rules against its live page; the application and renewal PDFs have no fillable fields; no staff names or personal mailboxes are recorded (revenue@ci.staunton.va.us is the office mailbox printed on the Commissioner's own forms and instructions); ids are unique and every form id a step cites exists.
open_issues: The city site (www.ci.staunton.va.us) still refuses the research client (HTTP 403), so every city page and PDF was read from Internet Archive copies of September 2025 to August 2026, not live. The 2027 renewal form will carry new dates. This does not change any step, but the pages should be confirmed live.

Staunton City Code Chapter 5.05, Article II, beyond § 5.05.170 as the city page reproduces it, was not read (eCode360 terms forbid copying). The ordinance's own due date, penalty, interest, extension and appeal sections are not known; the $30 fee and the $50,000 floor come from the city's forms. The steps rest on the forms and on state law, which every BPOL ordinance must follow in substance (§ 58.1-3703.1(A)).

The city publishes no classification-appeal procedures, or name and address for appeals, on its website, although § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(c) requires them; the escalation route is built from state law and assumes appeals go to the Commissioner of the Revenue.

How the tax is computed just above $50,000 (on all gross receipts, as the ordinance text and the application's note say, or only above $50,000) is not settled by any source read; s5 follows the application's instruction.
Whether Staunton's wholesale merchant rates, above the 5 cents per $100 cap in § 58.1-3716, are grandfathered from January 1, 1964 was not checked.
Staunton's population is close to 25,000, the line that sets the fee cap and the $50,000 floor; the city's $30 fee is within either cap.
The Home Occupation Permit fee and application were not confirmed (the fee schedule has no home occupation line; the application PDF could not be read).
